job_statement: When I need to connect my source code repository to the pipeline system, I want to create a Repository CR that matches incoming events to my repository URL, so I can automatically trigger pipeline runs when code changes occur
desired_outcomes: Minimize the time required to set up repository event handling
Ensure that events are matched to the correct namespace
Prevent unauthorized pipeline execution in other namespaces
evidence: using-repository-crd.adoc → Lines 76-103: Creating the Repository custom resource. The section describes how to create a Repository CR using tkn pac CLI or kubectl to match events from a repository URL and trigger pipeline runs in the target namespace.
notes: This is the foundational setup job for Pipelines as Code. The section includes important security notes about namespace targeting and preventing malicious actors from executing pipelines in unauthorized namespaces.

section: Creating the global Repository custom resource
job_statement: When I need to apply common settings across all repositories in my organization, I want to create a global Repository CR with default configurations, so I can avoid repeating the same settings in every repository-specific CR
parent_job: When I need to connect my source code repository to the pipeline system, I want to create a Repository CR that matches incoming events to my repository URL, so I can automatically trigger pipeline runs when code changes occur
prerequisites: Have administrator access to the openshift-pipelines namespace
Log in to the OpenShift cluster using oc CLI
related_jobs: Manage common secrets for repository access
desired_outcomes: Minimize repetition of common configuration across multiple repositories
Ensure consistent authentication settings across all repositories
Reduce administrative overhead when onboarding new repositories
evidence: using-repository-crd.adoc → Lines 113-164: Creating the global Repository custom resource. The section explains how to create a Repository CR named 'pipeline-as-code' in the openshift-pipelines namespace to provide default settings (like GitLab secrets) that apply to all Repository CRs created subsequently.
notes: This is marked as Technology Preview. This is a variant approach to the basic Repository CR creation, focused on centralized configuration management. It's a user_story under the main job of setting up Repository CRs.

job_statement: When multiple pipeline runs could be triggered simultaneously for my repository, I want to limit the number of concurrent executions, so I can prevent resource exhaustion and ensure orderly processing of events
desired_outcomes: Minimize the risk of cluster resource exhaustion
Prevent concurrent pipeline runs from interfering with each other
evidence: using-repository-crd.adoc → Lines 173-196: Setting concurrency limits. The section describes using the concurrency_limit spec to define the maximum number of pipeline runs running simultaneously, with pipeline runs queued and started in alphabetical order when the limit is reached.
notes: This is a resource management and optimization job. The alphabetical ordering behavior is an important detail for understanding execution sequence.

section: Changing the source branch for the pipeline definition
job_statement: When I need to ensure pipeline definitions are reviewed before execution, I want to configure the Repository CR to fetch pipeline definitions from the default branch instead of the event-triggering branch, so I can enforce code review on all pipeline changes before they run
prerequisites: Merge pipeline definitions into default branch
desired_outcomes: Minimize the risk of executing unreviewed pipeline code
Ensure all pipeline changes undergo merge review
Prevent malicious pipeline definitions from running via pull requests
evidence: using-repository-crd.adoc → Lines 205-228: Changing the source branch for the pipeline definition. The section explains setting pipelinerun_provenance to 'default_branch' to fetch pipeline definitions from the default branch (main/master/trunk) rather than the triggering branch, with a note that this is a security precaution requiring merge reviews.
notes: This is primarily a security-focused configuration job. The note explicitly calls out the security motivation: preventing execution of unreviewed pipeline definitions from pull requests.

job_statement: When I need to inject environment-specific or administratively-controlled values into pipeline runs, I want to define custom parameters in the Repository CR that expand within PipelineRun resources, so I can manage configuration centrally without modifying pipeline definitions in Git
related_jobs: Manage Kubernetes secrets for sensitive parameters
Configure conditional parameter expansion with CEL filters
desired_outcomes: Minimize the need to modify pipeline definitions in Git for environment-specific values
Ensure sensitive parameters are managed outside of Git repositories
Enable different parameter values based on event type (push vs pull_request)
evidence: using-repository-crd.adoc → Lines 238-305: Custom parameter expansion. The section describes using the params field in Repository CR to define custom parameters (like registry URLs or account UUIDs) that expand in PipelineRun resources, with support for literal values, secret_ref values, and CEL-filtered conditional expansion.
notes: This is a configuration management job focused on separating environment-specific configuration from pipeline code. The note explicitly advises against using this when Tekton PipelineRun parameters would suffice, suggesting this is for admin-managed values that shouldn't be in Git.
